A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the MARINE research work despite retitling and substantial extensions. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CHAIR, POPE and GPT-4V evaluations across six LVLMs, plus guidance-strength, detector-threshold and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations and additional aggregation, prompting, adaptive-guidance, robustness, latency and memory experiments in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: v1 constructs guidance from a single DETR source. v2 adds explicit aggregation of multiple guidance models in Algorithm 1, implemented using DETR and RAM++ with synonym-based intersection. Appendix B.2 also introduces a confidence-adaptive guidance variant. The underlying two-branch logit combination remains unchanged, but guidance construction and its optional weighting procedure materially expand.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates MSCOCO captioning/object-presence tasks and LLaVA-QA90. v2 retains these and adds POPE evaluation on A-OKVQA and GQA image sets (Tables 4 and 16), substantially broadening the evaluated data. These additions concern object-presence probing rather than evaluation of the benchmarks' full native VQA tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds OPERA to the main CHAIR and POPE comparisons. VCD expands from two previously reported POPE model results to comparisons across five LVLMs and participation in CHAIR. Appendix B.1 adds direct-prompting and prompt-as-guidance controls. LURE-with-cutoff and the separate sampled Original rows are removed from the principal comparisons.

E3.justification: v1 specifies temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.9 for CHAIR; v2 makes greedy decoding the main setting. Its fixed guidance strength of 0.7 also replaces the 0.5 specified for v1's GPT-4V evaluation. LLaMA-Adapter-v2 is dropped, and GPT-4V evaluation narrows from six models to two. New protocols include random/popular POPE settings, general text-quality and ALOHa metrics, and latency/memory measurements.

E4.justification: v2 adds single-versus-combined detector and intersection-versus-union ablations, engineered-prompt controls, adaptive guidance, stochastic-decoding robustness, resource analyses and quantitative guidance/quality tradeoffs (Tables 6–7 and Appendix B). Earlier LLaVA/mPLUG-Owl2 threshold plots and the logit example are retained or relocated, while InstructBLIP sweeps and several qualitative judge examples disappear.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix A.2 reports means over seeds 42, 142 and 242 without dispersion. v2 specifies seed 242 for deterministic main evaluations, adds mean ± standard deviation for stochastic CHAIR results (Table 22), and adds ± entries to GPT-4V results (Table 3). The new run counts and meaning of the GPT-4V uncertainty entries are unspecified; increased replication cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Main results are extensively replaced: LLaVA's CHAIR (CS, CI, Recall) changes from (24.3, 7.1, 67.8) for v1 MARINE-DETR to (17.8, 7.2, 50.8) for v2 MARINE; POPE accuracy changes from 80.6 to 66.9 (Tables 1–2). Changed guidance and decoding settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains or losses. Numerous cross-dataset, ablation, efficiency and ALOHa results are added, while several model/judge result entries are removed.

T1.justification: The autoregressive factorization, Bayesian classifier-free-guidance derivation and logit-mixture equations remain substantively unchanged. Appendix B.2 newly defines confidence-dependent guidance through gamma' = 0.4 + 0.4(s - s_min)/(s_max - s_min). This is a limited mathematical definition added for the adaptive variant, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 makes multi-source image-grounded aggregation a central contribution and adds explicit claims of the lowest mitigation overhead and preserved general caption/VQA quality. The abstract narrows improved detailedness to maintained detailedness. Training-free, API-free inference-time hallucination mitigation remains the central objective, but the claimed contribution and advertised benefits materially expand.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations based on detector agreement and model-dependent adaptive guidance, explicit hallucination-metric limitations, and boundaries concerning other hallucinations and inherited language-model biases. Earlier guidance-strength and noise interpretations largely remain. Some new interpretations overgeneralize: Section 5.3 claims intersection consistently beats union, although Table 7 favors union on LLaVA-v1.5; Tables 17–18 also show some text-quality declines.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-release link, A6000 hardware specifications, per-model batch sizes, generation limits, detector thresholds, baseline hyperparameters, prompt templates and NLTK-based synonym integration (Appendix A). These substantially expand implementation documentation. Conversely, v1's exact GPT-4V snapshot and January 2024 evaluation dates are omitted. Newly disclosed settings do not establish that those settings changed in previously reported experiments.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix C.2 substantially expand positioning around OPERA, HALC, BRAVE and newer grounding, steering and evaluation approaches. Additional references support aggregation, benchmarks and metrics, while several diffusion-guidance references disappear. The positioning shifts from a novel multimodal classifier-free-guidance application toward a training-free, modular framework combining visual sources.

P1.justification: Beyond changing the title and MARINE acronym expansion, v2 extensively rewrites the introduction, contribution statement, method exposition and results narrative. Earlier logit, fine-tuning and detector-noise discussions move into reorganized Appendices A–C. References move before the supplement, and acknowledgments and an impact statement are added. This constitutes substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout, redraws the framework around multiple guidance models, restructures main tables with average columns and a smaller GPT-4V panel, and adds radar, efficiency and ablation displays. Retained case studies and logit panels are relocated or rearranged; the GPT-4V prompt figure becomes Table 15. These are substantial visual changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation: aggregation and prompting controls test the contribution of visual guidance, additional datasets and ALOHa reduce dependence on the original evaluation, and measured latency/memory plus implementation details make efficiency claims more assessable. Narrower model/GPT-4V coverage, incomplete uncertainty definitions and overstatements such as the interpretation of Table 7 are drawbacks. Nevertheless, the gains in experimental scrutiny and reproducibility substantially improve the paper overall.
